description: The Freight Analysis Framework integrates data from many sources into a picture of freight movement among US states and major metropolitan areas by all modes of transportation. Version 5 (FAF5) starts from the 2017 Commodity Flow Survey and Census Bureau international trade data and adds agriculture, extraction, utility, construction, service and other sectors, giving tonnage and value by region of origin and destination, commodity type and mode for base year 2017, with forecasts at five-year steps through 2050 under three economic growth scenarios. It is produced by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics and the Federal Highway Administration; FAF 6, a new benchmark based on 2022 data, is now published by BTS. Coverage is national, by FAF region, with truck flows assigned to a model highway network. Downloads are free: the full origin-destination database, highway assignment results for 2017, 2022 and 2050 (zip files of 529 to 713 MB), the model highway network, summary tables, a data tabulation tool and dashboards. Caveats: flows are modelled estimates, not observations, the FAQ now has a section on FAF limitations, and the ORNL tool host was intermittently unavailable on 26 September 2026. FAF supports network flow, capacity planning and resilience studies of freight corridors and supply chains, and relates to the Commodity Flow Survey and the HPMS road network catalogued here, both of which feed it.
